text.p: Clayton Williams Energy Inc said Tuesday it expects to report net income for 1996 of $13.2 million to $13.9 million, or $1.70 to $1.80 per share, compared with a net loss of $8.1 million, or $1.31 per share, for 1995.
Cash flow from operating activities is expected to be about $40 million in 1996, up from $24.2 million in 1995.
Proved oil and gas reserves at December 31, 1996, were estimated by independent engineers to be 8.5 million barrels of oil and 35.8 bcf of natural gas, the company said.

The company currently has three rigs drilling in its 117,000 net acre block in Burleson, Milam and Robertson Counties of east Texas and is evaluating recent drilling results in the southern portion of this block. In addition, it is evaluating opportunities for expanding its drilling activities into other areas of Texas and Louisiana.

Assuming continued favorable product prices and drilling results, the company has increased its planned 1997 capital expenditures by about 10 percent, to $46 million, excluding costs associated with its Cotton Valley play.

Clayton has been able to increase the acreage covered by its Cotton Valley 3-D seismic survey, from 20,000 to about 50,000 net acres, while increasing the estimated cost of the survey only $900,000, to about $4.0 million.

Clayton said it will continue to evaluate opportunities to expand the area covered by the survey, which could increase the survey's cost. Due to the additional acreage included in the survey, it expects completion during the third quarter, with any drilling resulting from the survey beginning in the fourth quarter.
